commit_message:
Harden ~/.config/prisma-platform/auth.json file permissions to 0o600

CredentialsStore.writeCredentialsToDisk writes the Prisma Platform OAuth
tokens (token + refreshToken per workspaceId) to the auth file via
writeFile(this.authFilePath, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)) with no mode
option. Node's default 0o666 masked by umask 022 gives 0o644 on macOS
Terminal and most Linux defaults, so the file ends up world-readable.
The surrounding directory was likewise being created at 0o755 via
mkdir(... { recursive: true }) with no mode.

Any local account or process that can traverse the home directory can
recover the token + refreshToken and call the Prisma Platform management
API as the user.

This commit:
- Adds `chmod` to the fs/promises imports.
- Passes `{ mode: 0o600 }` to writeFile and `{ mode: 0o700 }` to mkdir.
- Adds a follow-up chmod for both file and directory so pre-existing
  installs converge to 0o600/0o700 on the next save. Per Node docs,
  fs.chmod on Windows silently no-ops b

Harden ~/.config/prisma-platform/auth.json file permissions to 0o600

CredentialsStore.writeCredentialsToDisk writes the Prisma Platform OAuth
tokens (token + refreshToken per workspaceId) to the auth file via
writeFile(this.authFilePath, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)) with no mode
option. Node's default 0o666 masked by umask 022 gives 0o644 on macOS
Terminal and most Linux defaults, so the file ends up world-readable.
The surrounding directory was likewise being created at 0o755 via
mkdir(... { recursive: true }) with no mode.

Any local account or process that can traverse the home directory can
recover the token + refreshToken and call the Prisma Platform management
API as the user.

This commit:
- Adds `chmod` to the fs/promises imports.
- Passes `{ mode: 0o600 }` to writeFile and `{ mode: 0o700 }` to mkdir.
- Adds a follow-up chmod for both file and directory (wrapped in
  try/catch for Windows) so pre-existing installs converge to 0o600/0o700
  on the next save.

ORM iteration has slowed enough that the nightly test matrix and the
half-hourly BuildPulse analytics upload are no longer worth the CI spend.

so they remain manually runnable. The `schedule:` blocks are commented
out (not deleted) so re-enabling is a one-PR uncomment when ORM
iteration resumes. `test.yml` itself is untouched — push/PR-triggered
CI keeps running on `main`.

at a workflow on a different repo whose schedule is being disabled in
the same coordinated effort, and once that schedule is off, the badge
would freeze at whatever colour it had on disable day. Risks
broadcasting a stale-red signal indefinitely. The `Prisma Tests Status`
badge stays — it's driven by push, not cron, and won't rot.

fix(adapters): preserve constraint name in UniqueConstraintViolation error mapping for Postgres-based adapters

When a unique constraint violation (23505) occurs on PostgreSQL, the
constraint name (error.constraint) was previously dropped by adapter-pg,
adapter-neon, and adapter-ppg. Only fields extracted from the detail
message were preserved, which is ambiguous for partial unique indexes
where multiple constraints share the same key columns.

This change preserves the constraint name as { index: error.constraint }
when available, falling back to fields-based extraction otherwise. The
pattern already existed for ForeignKeyConstraintViolation (23503) in all
three adapters, and adapter-mariadb already uses { index } for 1062.

Closes #29495

fix(bootstrap): add scripted mode, reorder deps, capture subprocess errors

Three changes to make `prisma bootstrap` work reliably in non-interactive
environments (AI agents, CI) and improve diagnostics:

1. Scripted mode: when both `--api-key` and `--database` are provided,
   all `confirm()` prompts are auto-accepted. In an empty directory,
   defaults to the `nextjs` template. This removes the TTY requirement
   that caused hangs in Claude Code / Cursor agents.

2. Deps-before-link: the dependency gate (dotenv, prisma, @prisma/client)
   now runs before the link step. Previously, if link failed after init
   but before deps were installed, re-running `prisma bootstrap` crashed
   with "Cannot find module 'dotenv/config'" at config load time.

3. Subprocess stderr capture: `runLocalPrismaCommand` now uses `spawn`
   with a piped stderr stream instead of `execFileSync` with inherited
   stdio. This captures stderr for telemetry while still displaying it
   to the user, and propagates

commit_message:
fix(docker): make MongoDB replica set init idempotent

The replica-set init script in the shared MongoDB Dockerfile uses
`until ($MONGO_COMMAND ... rs.initiate(...)); do sleep 1; done` to
wait for mongod to become ready before seeding the replica set. On
first boot this works correctly.

However, when the container is restarted (`docker restart`, `docker
compose up -d` after a stop, host reboot, etc.) with its writable
layer still intact, the replica set config already exists in the data
directory. `rs.initiate()` then returns an `AlreadyInitialized`
error (code 23) with a non-zero exit status, which the `until` loop
treats as "not ready yet" and retries every second, forever. Each
iteration spawns a fresh mongosh process (heavy JS startup) and opens
several connections to mongod, pinning one CPU core and accumulating
hundreds of thousands of leaked connections over time.

Wrap the `rs.initiate(...)` call in a JS try/catch that swallows
only the `AlreadyInitialized` case (by `codeName`

commit_message:
fix(client-engine-runtime): surface unmapped driver errors as user-facing P2039

When a driver adapter error arrived with `kind: 'postgres'` (or `mysql` /
`sqlite` / `mssql`) and the adapter did not map the underlying database
error code to a more specific `MappedError` kind, `rethrowAsUserFacing`
rethrew the raw `DriverAdapterError` unchanged.

Locally, that surfaced as `PrismaClientUnknownRequestError`. Worse, the
query plan executor returned HTTP 500 with the real error message in the
body, and Accelerate strips 500 response bodies, so end users only saw a
generic P6000 with no way to diagnose the underlying problem.

This commonly happens on schema drift — e.g. an `upsert()` targeting a
column whose unique index was dropped in the DB raises Postgres 42P10
("there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT
specification"), which is not individually mapped by the adapter. These
errors are not bugs and end users need to see the underlying DB code and
message to debu

fix(adapter-libsql): handle socket errors wrapped in HRANA_WEBSOCKET_ERROR

@libsql/client wraps raw socket errors (ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND, etc.)
inside a LibsqlError with code HRANA_WEBSOCKET_ERROR and the original
error in `cause`. The previous isSocketError check only inspected the
top-level error.code, so these wrapped errors fell through to isDriverError
and were returned as { kind: 'sqlite', extendedCode: 1 } instead of the
correct DatabaseNotReachable / ConnectionClosed / SocketTimeout kind.

Fix: introduce isRawSocketError for the leaf check and make isSocketError
also inspect error.cause, then extract the right error in mapSocketError.
Add unit test cases covering the wrapped-error path.

commit_message:
fix(adapter-mssql): handle socket errors that bypass isDriverError

Socket errors (ENOTFOUND, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT) from the
mssql driver lack the numeric `error.number` field required by
isDriverError, so they fell through to `throw error` unwrapped rather
than being returned as typed MappedError values (DatabaseNotReachable,
ConnectionClosed, SocketTimeout).

Added isSocketError guard checked before isDriverError, matching the
pattern used in adapter-pg, adapter-neon, and adapter-libsql.

Also adds errors.test.ts covering the major error code mappings and all
four socket error codes.

commit_message:
fix(adapter-libsql): handle socket errors before isDriverError check

Socket errors (ENOTFOUND, ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT) satisfy
the LibsqlError type guard — they have a string `code`, string `message`,
and undefined `rawCode` — so they slipped through `isDriverError` and
were returned as `{ kind: 'sqlite', extendedCode: 1 }` instead of the
correct `DatabaseNotReachable`, `ConnectionClosed`, or `SocketTimeout`.

The fix mirrors the pattern used in adapter-pg and adapter-neon: check
`isSocketError` before `isDriverError` to short-circuit before the
SQLite dispatch table.

commit_message:
fix(adapter-neon): handle TLS and socket errors in convertDriverError

adapter-neon's convertDriverError had no handling for Node.js TLS or
socket errors. When a WebSocket/TLS connection to the Neon server fails
(e.g. invalid cert, DNS lookup failure, connection refused), the error
reached the final `throw error` in convertDriverError and propagated as
a raw Node.js Error instead of a typed Prisma error like
TlsConnectionError, DatabaseNotReachable, ConnectionClosed, or
SocketTimeout.

adapter-pg handles all of these via isTlsError, isSocketError, and
their respective mapping functions. This PR brings adapter-neon to
parity.

Changes:
- Add TLS_ERRORS set (same Node.js TLS codes as adapter-pg)
- Add SOCKET_ERRORS set and isSocketError guard
- Add isTlsError guard (code-based; the pg-specific message checks do
  not apply to @neondatabase/serverless)
- mapSocketError: ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED → DatabaseNotReachable,
  ECONNRESET → ConnectionClosed, ETIMEDOUT → SocketTimeout
- Also include

fix(adapter-neon): use error.column for NullConstraintViolation and fix ColumnNotFound for unquoted names

PostgreSQL NOT NULL violations (23502) populate `error.column` with the
violating column name. The `error.detail` field contains
"Failing row contains (...)" — not the "Key (...)" format used by
unique-violation (23505) — so the regex that was used never matched,
causing `meta.target` to always be empty ([]) for P2011 errors.

Fix by reading `error.column` directly, consistent with adapter-pg.

For ColumnNotFound (42703), the old implementation
(`error.message.split(' ').at(1)?.split('"').at(1)`) only handled
quoted column names. The improved regex
(`/^column (.+) does not exist$/`) handles unquoted names, qualified
names, and escaped quotes, matching what adapter-pg already does since
#29307.

Adds an errors.test.ts covering all cases for both error codes.

commit_message:
fix(adapter-pg): use error.column for NullConstraintViolation constraint field

PostgreSQL's 23502 (NOT NULL violation) error sets `error.column` directly to the
violating column name. The previous implementation applied the regex
`/Key \(([^)]+)\)/` to `error.detail`, which is the unique-violation (23505) format.
For NOT NULL errors, `detail` contains "Failing row contains (...)" which never
matches that pattern, so `constraint` was always `undefined` and `meta.target` was
never populated for P2011 errors.

Fix: read `error.column` instead of parsing `error.detail`.

Updated the existing test to use real PostgreSQL error data (detail = "Failing row
contains ...", column = "foo") and added a second test for the case where
`error.column` is absent.

Fixes: https://github.com/prisma/prisma/issues (P2011 meta.target always empty)

fix(adapter-mariadb): ensure TIMESTAMP reads and writes use UTC regardless of server timezone

Two related bugs caused incorrect DateTime values when the MariaDB/MySQL
session timezone is not UTC:

**Write bug**: `formatDateTime` emitted no timezone suffix, so a TIMESTAMP
write was interpreted in the session's local timezone instead of UTC.
Fix: append `+00:00` so the TIMESTAMP column always receives an explicit
UTC value.  DATETIME columns ignore timezone suffixes, so this is a no-op
for those columns.

**Read bug**: `mapRow` appended 'Z' to every datetime string, treating it
as UTC.  But when the session timezone is non-UTC the string returned by
the driver (via `dateStrings: true`) is in the session's local timezone,
so treating it as UTC silently shifts the value by the offset.
Fix: `PrismaMariaDbAdapterFactory` now injects `timezone: '+00:00'` into
the pool config (object path) and URL (string path) so the driver always
returns UTC strings, making the `Z`-append in `mapRow` correc

commit_message:
fix(client-engine-runtime): populate meta.target for P2002 and P2011 errors

The Rust query engine populates `meta.target` on P2002 (UniqueConstraintViolation)
and P2011 (NullConstraintViolation) errors so that callers can identify which
field(s) caused the constraint violation. The JS driver-adapter runtime path was
throwing those errors with `meta` containing only `driverAdapterError`, leaving
`meta.target` always undefined.

`extractMeta` now reads the structured constraint information already present in
the DriverAdapterError and maps it to the standard `meta.target` field:
- When the adapter resolved field names (e.g. adapter-pg parses the PG error
  detail), `target` is set to that `string[]`.
- When the adapter only has an index name (e.g. adapter-mariadb, adapter-mssql),
  `target` is set to `[indexName]` so callers always get a consistent type.

The existing `driverAdapterError` meta key is preserved for backward compatibility.

Fixes #29344

commit_message:
fix(adapters): serialize JSON args with Decimal-aware replacer

`Decimal.prototype.toJSON` returns the string representation of the value,
so `JSON.stringify({ n: new Decimal("42") })` produces `{"n":"42"}` (a JSON
string) rather than the expected `{"n":42}` (a JSON number).

Each driver adapter's `mapArg` now pre-serialises JSON arguments using a
custom replacer that converts Decimal-like instances (detected by constructor
name and the presence of `toNumber`) to their numeric value before the
underlying driver library gets a chance to call `JSON.stringify` itself.

Also adds the missing `'JSON'` decltype case in adapter-libsql so that
columns declared as `JSON` are mapped to `ColumnTypeEnum.Json` (only `JSONB`
was handled before).

Fixes #29387

commit_message:
fix(adapter-mariadb): handle SET column type in mapColumnType and mapRow

MariaDbColumnType.SET was defined in the enum but not handled in
mapColumnType, causing it to throw "Unsupported column type: SET" for
any schema that maps a MariaDB/MySQL SET column.

Additionally, the mariadb connector can return SET column values as a
JavaScript Array when multiple values are active. mapRow now normalises
these to a comma-joined string, consistent with the Text column type
returned by mapColumnType and with how MySQL SET values are represented
in Prisma (String? / @db.Set()).

Fixes #29398

commit_message:
fix(adapter-pg): add missing TIMETZ_ARRAY (OID 1270) type mapping

TIMETZ[] columns were not handled in fieldToColumnType or customParsers.
Because OID 1270 (_timetz) is below FIRST_NORMAL_OBJECT_ID (16384), the
default branch threw UnsupportedNativeDataType, surfacing as a P2010 error:

  "Failed to deserialize column of type 'Unknown'."

Fix:
- Add TIMETZ_ARRAY: 1270 to ArrayColumnType constants
- Handle it in fieldToColumnType returning ColumnTypeEnum.TimeArray
  (consistent with the existing TIME_ARRAY case)
- Register normalize_array(normalize_timez) in customParsers so the
  timezone offset is stripped from each element, matching the scalar
  TIMETZ behaviour

Fixes #29397

commit_message:
fix(client-engine-runtime): serialize join children inside transactions

When `update` (or any write) with `include` relations is executed inside a
transaction, the `join` node in the query interpreter fires a `Promise.all`
over all child relation fetches. Each child eventually calls `queryRaw` on
`context.queryable`, which — inside a transaction — is a single `pg.PoolClient`
(not a pool). Concurrent `client.query()` calls on a single pg Client trigger:

  "Calling client.query() when the client is already executing a query is
  deprecated and will be removed in pg@9.0."

This becomes a hard error in pg@9.0.

Fix: detect whether `context.queryable` is a `Transaction` (via the `commit`
property on the `Transaction` interface) and, if so, fetch the join children
sequentially instead of in parallel. When using a connection pool the existing
parallel behaviour is preserved.

Fixes #29407

commit_message:
refactor(migrate): remove deprecated shadowDatabaseUrl from MigrateDiffInput

Companion to prisma/prisma-engines#5803. The shadow database URL is
now exclusively configured via `datasource.shadowDatabaseUrl` in
`prisma.config.ts`, and the `DiffParams.shadow_database_url` field
has been removed from the schema engine.

This removes the matching `shadowDatabaseUrl` field from the
TypeScript `MigrateDiffInput` interface and the hardcoded `null`
value passed in `MigrateDiff.parse()`.

Fixes #29454

fix(cli): bootstrap UX — auto-install deps, resumable flow, timeout handling (#29424)

/integration

## Summary

Addresses product testing feedback
([PTL-1372](https://linear.app/prisma-company/issue/PTL-1372)) for
`prisma bootstrap`:

- **Template download timeout** — increased from 30s to 120s. Added
proper error handling on `nodeStream` in `decompressGzip` to prevent
unhandled `DOMException` crashes on Node 25. Timeout errors now show a
user-friendly message.
- **Auto-install missing deps** — instead of dead-ending with "install
manually and re-run", the command now prompts to install missing
`dotenv`/`prisma` via the detected package manager (`npm`, `pnpm`,
`yarn`, `bun`).
- **Resumable re-run** — when `--database` is passed on an

   Existing projects go straight to prisma init with the sample model
   prompt. Explicit --template flag still works on existing projects.

3. Extract scaffoldTemplate() helper to avoid duplication.

commit_message:
fix(client-engine-runtime): serialize unknown driver adapter error cause as JSON

When a driver adapter throws an error with an unrecognised `cause.kind`
(e.g. a newer adapter version talking to an older client), `assertNever`
built its message with a template-literal that coerced the cause object to
a string, producing the unhelpful "Unknown error: [object Object]".

Replace the bare interpolation with `safeJsonStringify` (already present in
`./utils`) so the full cause object is serialised in the thrown message.

Adds a unit test that verifies the message contains the serialised kind and
never degrades to "[object Object]".

Fixes #29310

fix(bootstrap): UX fixes for resumable flow, auto-install deps, timeout handling

- Increase template download timeout from 30s to 120s for slow connections
- Add error handler on nodeStream in decompressGzip to prevent unhandled error crashes (Node 25)
- Show user-friendly message for timeout errors instead of raw DOMException
- Replace dead-end "install deps manually" gate with interactive prompt to
  install missing deps via detected package manager
- Fix re-run dead-end: when --database is passed on an already-linked project,
  skip link step and continue to migrate/generate/seed instead of blocking
- Only list actually missing deps in the prompt (not all checked deps)
- Update tests to cover new auto-install behavior

Fixes PTL-1372

Extracts the parameterization logic into `client-engine-runtime` from
`client`. The purpose is to make it more easily consumable from query
engine tests. I've also extracted some DMMF logic into a new package
called `get-dmmf`, the code was refactored to avoid using `fp-ts` and
written with plain `try ... catch` instead.

Remove dead code from `JsValue::Binary` in `is_truthy` (#94165)

This is another thing flagged by @bgw's Claude:

```
  3. Dead duplicate match arm in is_truthy for StrictEqual (lines 2469–2494)

  ( … StrictEqual, Constant(a), Constant(b)) if a.is_value_type() => Some(a ==
  b),
  ( … StrictEqual, Constant(a), Constant(b)) if a.is_value_type() => { /* 
  same-type check */ }

  Identical pattern + guard. The second arm — the only one that handles
  cross-type equality conservatively — is unreachable. Looks like a half-applied
   fix.
``` 

I've removed the second arm with a double type check. Tests appear to
still pass and I can't think of a case where we'd hit the second arm.

commit_message:
Phase 1a: create empty turbo-tasks-handle crate

This crate is the future home of the #[no_mangle] pub extern "Rust"
fn providers that implement the dispatch surface declared (later in
this phase) in turbo-tasks/src/handle.rs.

For now it is a skeleton: lib.rs is empty (just a doc comment) and
the crate exposes two optional features:
  - prod : pulls in turbo-tasks-backend (will emit __tt_prod_*
    providers).
  - test : pulls in turbo-tasks-testing (will emit __tt_test_*
    providers).

Building with neither feature compiles to an empty lib, so 'cargo
check --workspace' works without flags. Binaries and tests that
actually consume the dispatch must enable the appropriate feature(s).

Update `shortcircuit_if_known` to `eval_shortcircuit()` (#94163)

Originally this PR was a comment fix that was flagged by @bgw's Claude:

```

  ▎ "Otherwise returns None."

  The function actually returns item_value(last_item) when no element matches.
  Comment doesn't describe behavior.

  ---
  The two most consequential bugs are #1 (swapped AND/OR predicates) and #2 
  (regex). #1 silently produces wrong nullishness/string-ness results for any
  code path that asks about &&/|| chains and feeds into linker decisions; #2
  silently corrupts every default-filter require.context resolution.
``` 

Related to #94159, updates the comment to say that it returns the last
item.

Which appears to be what is happening:

```rust
if it.peek().is_none() {
    return item_value(item);
} 
```

Afterwards, it now includes a reworking of `shortcircuit_if_known` into
`eval_shortcircuit()`:
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/94163#discussion_r3313537931

Turbopack's analyzer: always treat promises as truth-y and non-nullish (#94186)

Promises are not included in the list of JavaScript's falsy values,
therefore, they are always truthy. See
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Truthy. Additionally,
promises are neither `null` or `undefined` so they are not nullish:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Nullish_coalescing.

This PR updates Turbopack's analyzer to reflect this + adds unit tests
for `is_truthy` and `is_nullish`.

perf: use createElement instead of createElementNS for HTML elements (#18262)

## Summary

The current wrapper always calls `document.createElementNS(namespace ??
NAMESPACE_HTML, tag, options)` — even for HTML elements (the >99% case),
and even when `options` would be `undefined`. Two effects compound:

1. **Route HTML elements through `createElement`** — Blink has a fast
path that skips the namespace lookup `createElementNS` always performs.
2. **Omit the trailing `undefined` argument** — V8/Blink take a slower
path for `createElementNS(ns, tag, undefined)` (and `createElement(tag,
undefined)`) than for the bare 2-arg form. This applies symmetrically to
the SVG/MathML branch, where the wrapper now also avoids the `undefined`
3rd arg.

The wrapper dispatches to the fastest call shape for every input —
`{HTML, non-HTML}` × `{with is, without is}` × no `undefined` ever.

## Affects

Every place Svelte constructs a DOM element internally:
`<svelte:element>`, `run_scripts`, the per-compone

docs: add auto-generated browser support page (#18276)

## Summary

Adds a [Browser
support](https://github.com/MathiasWP/svelte/blob/document-pipeline-draft/documentation/docs/07-misc/05-browser-support.md)
page listing the minimum browser versions Svelte's runtime and compiler
output require. The page (headline floor + per-feature requirements) is
auto-generated by `packages/svelte/scripts/generate-browser-support.js`,
which scans the code Svelte actually ships against the
[web-features](https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features) Baseline
dataset and resolves results to concrete browser versions via
[baseline-browser-mapping](https://github.com/web-platform-dx/baseline-browser-mapping).
CI fails if a PR moves the floor without regenerating the page.

For 5.55.9 the floor is **Baseline 2020**: Chrome/Edge 87, Firefox 83,
Safari 14.

## How it works

1. **Headline floor.** Each runtime entry from `pkg.exports` is bundled
with rollup using production conditions, then walked with T

chore: replace custom renderer type arguments with a single one (#18244)

Alternative to #18216

Allows for inference to still works but also allow for explicit
declaration in the cases where it's needed.

I made some changes to the code proposed by @mrkishi (I used `unique
symbol` for the `DefaultType`, inferred the `NodeType`) but overall is
mostly his work.

I've also replaced the renderer for the test with a `TS` version of it
so we can better test the types there.

I think this is the best middle ground solution...inference works (when
it works...we can document that you need to put the create methods first
and the gotchas of automatic inference) but people can also quickly
specify their types in an object.

perf: store current_sources as Set for O(1) membership checks (#18278)

`current_sources` tracks the sources created within the active reaction
so that reading or writing them during that same reaction doesn't
trigger a re-run. It was an `Array` checked with
`Array.prototype.includes.call(...)` in three hot places: the
`state_unsafe_mutation` guard, `set()`'s destruction check, and
`schedule_possible_effect_self_invalidation`.

fix: prevent batch unlinking twice (#18303)

Merged #18298 a bit too soon - there's still a situation which can
corrput the linked list: If we merge one batch into another, it will
unlink the batch immediately. But `discard` also calls it, running the
unlink logic again, which can corrupt the linked list.

Sketch:

1. Batch A is pending.
2. Batch B starts later, intersects A, resolves first, and merges into
A.
3. B is unlinked immediately, but `A.oncommit(() => B.discard())`
remains.
4. Independent batch C is created while A is still pending and is linked
after A.
5. A commits, calls `B.discard()`, and B's stale `#prev`/`#next` can set
`A.#next = null` / `last_batch = A`, disconnecting C.

Not able to produce a failing test from it but it's definitely a fix we
need to make.

Also moved `#link` into a constructor, because it is (and should be)
used only once.

Also made the action after an error `discard` instead of just `#unlink`
because this batch is done for and e.g. pending `settled

fix: disallow effect creation after `await` (#18299)

We incorrectly restore effect context after an`$derived(await ...)` if
it occurs inside an async function, but only for those, no other `await`
expressions. This is buggy and wrong. We only want to restore context
_inside_ an async derived expression (including template expressions)`
so that `await a + b` works correctly.

It's possible that this will be a breaking change (albeit not
semver-violating, because `experimental`) for some people if they are
creating effects after an `await` (other than at the top level of a
component). This is regrettable, but it should never have worked in the
first place.

fix: reject pending async deriveds on discard

The rejects all async deriveds of a batch as `OBSOLETE`, so they don't hang around and bail early without triggering the batch.

If we don't do this, an async derived can trigger the already done batch, which schedules an effect that is never flushed. Because it is never flushed the branches it touched on its way up are never cleared, and so anything else in that subtree is now unreactive.

perf: use Set instead of Array for constant lookups in utils.js (#18250)

Several constant lookup tables in `utils.js` were arrays searched with
`Array.prototype.includes`, which is O(n). They're queried often — per
attribute during attribute setup and SSR, per event during event
delegation, and per identifier during compilation. Switching them to
`Set` makes each lookup O(1) without changing any public behaviour.

perf: store current_sources as Set for O(1) membership checks

The per-reaction collection of "sources created within this reaction" is
checked on every signal write inside a reaction (set, dev-mode
state_unsafe_mutation guard) and on every self-invalidation scheduling
pass. With Array.includes the check was O(n); switching to a Set makes
it O(1) and also drops the bound-call indirection of `includes.call`.

No semantic change: the collection is still per-reaction, still saved
and restored across nested reactions, still seeded by push_reaction_value.

fix: remove raw-text hydration markers (#18269)

Fixes #14413.

This keeps the temporary raw-text hydration sentinel used by dynamic

gets a marker to advance through for raw-text children, but the marker
is removed after the child renderer runs, so `<style>` and `<script>`
contents stay identical to SSR output.

commit_message:
fix: declare `let:` directives before `{@const}` on slotted elements

When a `let:` directive sits on a slotted element (e.g. `<tr slot="row" let:row>`),
its derived declaration was pushed onto the element's `init` statements, which the
Fragment emits after `{@const}` declarations. A sibling `{@const}` that captured the
slot prop therefore referenced it before initialization, throwing "Cannot access
'...' before initialization" in dev mode (where the const is read eagerly).

Route the `let:` declarations into `let_directives` instead so they precede the
`{@const}` declarations, matching how component-level `let:` directives are handled.

perf: walk composedPath() directly in delegated event propagation (#18268)

## Summary

The propagation walk in `handle_event_propagation` already calls
`event.composedPath()` at the start to find the entry index, but then
re-derives the same chain step-by-step via `current_target.assignedSlot
|| current_target.parentNode || .host`. Three property reads per
iteration is measurable on the hot event path.

Walk the captured `path` array by index instead.

## Notes on behavior

`composedPath()` is the spec-compliant snapshot of the dispatch chain:
- Same shadow-DOM crossings (slots and shadow roots are included for
composed events).
- Same `host` traversal (composed-path crosses shadow boundaries when
appropriate).
- Differs from the previous walk in one edge case: if a handler removes
a parent mid-dispatch, the snapshot-based walk continues through the
captured chain (matches native browser semantics — the previous
`parentNode` walk would have stopped at a null parent).

## Performance

fix: catch rejected promises while merging/committing (#18266)

A committing/merging batch can have promises that were rejected (e.g. as
obsolete). We gotta "forward" this rejection, too, instead of just the
successful promise. At best it results in a uncaught rejection
(`async-branch-merge-obsolete`), at worst it means error boundaries are
not correctly displayed (`async-later-promise-fails-first`).

Solves the reproduction in
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4507803845

fix: unlink errored and otherwise finished batch (#18264)

This fixes the issue in
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414
where an error can create follup-up invariant errors. The batch errors,
has no chance to run otherwise (no more pending work) and is therefore
"dead". That means we need to unlink it otherwise it's becoming a
"zombie" and hangs around, causing unnecessary and potentially buggy (as
seen in the reproduction) merge/commit work.

I was not able to reduce the reproduction down to a test case that fails
without the fix, but it does make a related error test from #17888 work
more correctly.

commit_message:
fix: make unnecessary commit work less likely (#18263)

While looking at
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414
and trying to understand how the invariant can happen I noticed that we
are not correctly filtering during commit.
- we were not ignoring deriveds
- we were not comparing the correct values (checking `source.v` instead
of the saved value) and not checking if their "is a derived" state
differs

I'm not able to come up with a test where something fails without these
(possibly because it's more about an optimization to do less reruns and
not about correctness) fixes, but they do make sense.

commit_message:
fix: correctly coordinate component-level effects inside async blocks (#18260)

While looking at the reproduction in
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414
I immediately got greeted with a runtime error when running it in the
playground (weirdly not in the Stackblitz version). The error was that a
component expected a binding to be set in onMount, but the timing of
onMount was wrong.

Turns out it's because our logic to determine whether or not to defer
top level effects is flawed. `REACTION_RAN`, which was used previously,
is already set if the initialized component is inside an async block. We
instead check for `component_context.i` which is set to `true` on
`pop()`.

- `tsgo`/`tsc` against the test code failed with TS2775 across ~165

  TypeScript requires the call target to be explicitly annotated, but the

  `ok`/`snapshot` properties to the test callback.

  routing isn't reliable in CI's forks pool. Move error capture to the
  window-error listener directly: switch to c

commit_message:
perf: batch FLIP animation reads and writes

Split the per-item `fix()` step in the keyed `{#each}` animation manager
into three phases (`fix_size` reads only, `fix_position` writes only,
`fix_transform` reads the post-absolute rect and applies a compensating
transform). The caller in each.js runs three batched loops instead of one
combined loop, which cuts forced synchronous reflows from ~2N down to ~2
per destroy batch.

The visual result is unchanged: `transform = from - to` lands the element
at its captured `from` position regardless of when `to` is measured.

Measured ~+42% in real Chromium on a 45-item animate:flip destroy.
All 6006 runtime tests still pass.

commit_message:
chore: upgrade vitest to 4.1.7

Bumps vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 from ^2.1.9 to ^4.1.7. Three
test-harness updates compensate for vitest 4 behavior changes:

- runtime-browser/test.ts: vitest 4 removed the deprecated `describe(name,
  fn, opts)` signature; pass options as the second argument.
- runtime-legacy/shared.ts: vitest 4's jsdom env binds `virtualConsole`
  to the original `globalThis.console` before vitest wraps it, so
  inline-`<script>` logs and `jsdomError` events no longer reach per-test
  `console.{log,error}` overrides. Re-route the virtual console through
  the live console in `beforeAll`. Also promote the window-error listener
  to a named function and remove it in `finally` so listeners from
  earlier tests no longer leak and write to `unhandled_rejection`.

commit_message:
narrow the LIS pass with a backward suffix walk

The prior pass diverged on first mismatch and then ran LIS over the entire
suffix `[i_start, length)` — fine for big reorders (reverse, shuffle), but
expensive on small ones where most of the tail was actually stable. In a
real-browser benchmark a single far swap regressed ~27% vs the legacy
heuristic because the LIS bookkeeping (Map allocations, the LIS sequence
itself, chain rebuild) dominated for an O(2) move workload.

Walk forward AND backward to identify the stable prefix and suffix in
lockstep, then run LIS only over the unstable middle. Falls back to the
legacy heuristic when the walks expose an add/remove (length mismatch in
the middle), an INERT/offscreen entry, or a non-branch sibling effect —
same eligibility rules as before.

Measured in real Chromium (Chromium 145) via the browser bench harness in
#18261:

|             | baseline | prior LIS | new LIS  |     vs heuristic     |
| ----------- | -------: | --------: | -------

fix: unlink errored and otherwise finished batch

This fixes the issue in https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414 where an error can create follup-up invariant errors. I was not able to reduce the reproduction down to a test case that fails without the fix, but it does make a related error test from #17888 work more correctly.

fix: make unnecessary commit work less likely

While looking at https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414 and trying to understand how the invariant can happen I noticed that we are not correctly filtering during commit.

I'm not able to come up with a test where something fails without these (possibly because it's more about an optimization to do less reruns and not about correctness) fixes, but they do make sense.

commit_message:
fix: correctly coordinate component-level effects inside async blocks

While looking at the reproduction in https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/18221#issuecomment-4497918414 I immediately got greeted with a runtime error when running it in the playground (weirdly not in the Stackblitz version). The error was that a component expected a binding to be set in onMount, but the timing of onMount was wrong.

Turns out it's because our logic to determine whether or not to defer top level effects is flawed. `REACTION_RAN`, which was used previously, is already set if the initialized component is inside an async block. We instead check for `component_context.i` which is set to `true` on `pop()`.

commit_message:
perf(each): minimise DOM moves in keyed reconciliation via LIS fast path

For pure-reorder updates of a keyed `{#each}` block — no additions, removals,
transitions, async items, or non-branch sibling effects — we now take a
longest-increasing-subsequence pass that produces the minimum number of DOM
moves. A lockstep pre-check handles the no-reorder case (reactive text/attribute
update on existing rows) without allocating anything; only on first divergence
do we build the data structures for the LIS pass. Everything else falls through
to the existing heuristic, so no behaviour changes outside the fast path.

| dom_swap_rows     |    50ms |   48ms  |  −4%  |
| dom_update_row    |    14ms |   13ms  |  ~0   |
| dom_create_rows   | ~1600ms | ~1600

fix: transfer effects when merging batches (#18254)

An effect could be gated behind a branch. If we don't defer + transfer
them upon merge, the branch would still be marked clean but the effect
behind it is dirty but no longer reachable. It's not reachable via mark
either because that one only concerns itself with block/async effects,
and the branch gating the effect is not guaranteed to be touched by
that.

Little sad side-effect: Since we cannot reliably know _before_ traversal
if we have no blocking pending work left (the traversal could mark an if
block falsy which contains the last blocker), we gotta undo a
performance optimization.

commit_message:
perf: hoist rest_props exclude list as a module-scope Set

The compiler emitted an inline string array as the second argument to
`$.rest_props(...)`. The runtime did a linear `Array.prototype.includes`
on this array on every property access via the rest-props Proxy.

The exclude list only depends on the component definition, not on the
instance, so it can be hoisted to module scope and shared by every
instance. Switching it to a `Set` at the same time makes each lookup
O(1).

For a component like `<Button ...rest />` rendered N times, this turns
one per-instance allocation (and N * E linear searches per access, where
E is the exclude size) into one module-scope allocation plus O(1)
lookups.

Thanks to
https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/issues/17940#issuecomment-4480016550

error. I had a hunch this could happen and this shows it. Essentially,
you can end up in situations where two batches are scheduled to run in
the same microtask queue flush, and if the first rebases the second the
invariant will throw, which is wrong. We can avoid this by checking if a
decrement is queued.

`{#await ...}` that deactivated a batch prior to reading the promise
function. That can result in a new batch being created if the promise
invocation happens to write a source.

SSR/hydration: On the server it would await the expression (which it
should not; `{#await await ...}` is kind of a weird special case here)
and during hydration it did not produce matching nodes, leading to
hydration fails.

the current reaction, we did not deduplicate those reads. That can lead
to duplicate dependencies, which in turn can lead to bugs when
`remove_reaction` later runs. Conside this: You have `deps = [count,
unrelated, count]`. Now you do `remove_reactions(deps, 1)`, i.e. "remove
all reactio

[ruby/rubygems] Vendor compact_index from rubygems.org for the artifice

The external compact_index gem is no longer developed; its source now
lives in rubygems/rubygems.org. Replace the runtime gem dependency with
a rake task that fetches the five files into tmp/compact_index/ when
`rake setup` (and therefore bin/setup) runs. The artifice loads from
that path instead of the staged gem install, which also gives us access
to the v2 GemVersion struct without waiting on an upstream release.

A small build_gem_version seam is added so subclassed artifices can
swap in the v2 struct on a per-test basis.

commit_message:
[ruby/rubygems] Move expired_cert tmp file into per-test @tempdir

Two re_sign tests wrote to a shared Dir.tmpdir/expired_cert.pem and
removed it in teardown, racing each other under test-unit
--parallel=process. @tempdir is already per-test and auto-cleaned,
so the manual @cleanup machinery goes away with the change.

https://github.com/ruby/rubygems/commit/4015ad5c76

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reserve 2 bits for expressing object layout

We would like to make instance variable reads in the JIT compiler faster
(as well as simplify the JIT implementation).  Currently, in order to
read an instance variable, we have to:

1. Test for heap object
2. Load object to a 64 bit register
3. Mask the object header
4. Bit test against the masked header
5. JNE
6. Load field

We would like to:

1. Test for heap object
2. Load object shape to a 32 bit register
3. Bit test against the shape
4. JNE
5. Load field

The way we fetch instance variables is not consistent across objects.
In order to realize our goal, we need to encode object layout inside the
shape.  If we encode object layout inside the shape, then the shape
itself will guarantee that the access pattern generated by the JIT
compiler is correct.

We should encode the following load patterns into the shape tag bits.
This way we can share shapes on transitions, but be able to
differentiate the access patterns for the JIT compiler.  In

commit_message:
Use stack callinfo/calldata for super dispatch

Previously vm_search_super_method would allocate a new callinfo and
write it back into the iseq's call data. Because iseqs can be shared
between Ractors (e.g. via Ractor.shareable_proc + define_method), two
Ractors invoking super through the same iseq could race on the ci/cc,
producing wrong dispatch or crashes from torn callcache reads on
weakly-ordered architectures.

Build the adjusted callinfo on the stack instead, mirroring
sendforward/invokesuperforward. The callcache is also loaded and stored
back with acquire/release atomics so it can be safely shared.

Reserve 2 bits for expressing object layout

We would like to make instance variable reads in the JIT compiler faster
(as well as simplify the JIT implementation).  Currently, in order to
read an instance variable, we have to:

1. Test for heap object
2. Load object to a 64 bit register
3. Mask the object header
4. Bit test against the masked header
5. JNE
6. Load field

We would like to:

1. Test for heap object
2. Load object shape to a 32 bit register
3. Bit test against the shape
4. JNE
5. Load field

The way we fetch instance variables is not consistent across objects.
In order to realize our goal, we need to encode object layout inside the
shape.  If we encode object layout inside the shape, then the shape
itself will guarantee that the access pattern generated by the JIT
compiler is correct.

We should encode the following load patterns into the shape tag bits.
This way we can share shapes on transitions, but be able to
differentiate the access patterns for the JIT compiler.  In

commit_message:
Reserve 2 bits for expressing object layout

We would like to make instance variable reads in the JIT compiler faster
(as well as simplify the JIT implementation).  Currently, in order to
read an instance variable, we have to:

1. Test for heap object
2. Load object to a 64 bit register
3. Mask the object header
4. Bit test against the masked header
5. JNE
6. Load field

We would like to:

1. Test for heap object
2. Load object shape to a 32 bit register
3. Bit test against the shape
4. JNE
5. Load field

The way we fetch instance variables is not consistent across objects.
In order to realize our goal, we need to encode object layout inside the
shape.  If we encode object layout inside the shape, then the shape
itself will guarantee that the access pattern generated by the JIT
compiler is correct.

We should encode the following load patterns into the shape tag bits.
This way we can share shapes on transitions, but be able to
differentiate the access patterns for the JIT compiler.  In

commit_message:
Use stack callinfo/calldata for super dispatch

Previously vm_search_super_method would allocate a new callinfo and
write it back into the iseq's call data. Because iseqs can be shared
between Ractors (e.g. via Ractor.shareable_proc + define_method), two
Ractors invoking super through the same iseq could race on the ci/cc,
producing wrong dispatch or crashes from torn callcache reads on
weakly-ordered architectures.

Build the adjusted callinfo on the stack instead, mirroring
sendforward/invokesuperforward. The callcache is also loaded and stored
back with acquire/release atomics so it can be safely shared.

[Bug #22084]

commit_message:
[hack] ZJIT: Insert NoEpEscape after each safepoint `Effect::write(abstract_heaps::Frame)`

This is a hacky fix for https://github.com/Shopify/ruby/issues/970.
I initially tried to do it as a pass, but then thought I wouldn't have
access to the right snapshots to construct a
`Invariant::NoEPEscape($snapshot_id)`, so I moved the logic to
iseq_to_hir. It's actually possible to find yarv insn boundaries
post-hoc by scanning backwards for snapshots -- they're present until
DCE. It's better to insert these PPs post-hoc, after strength reduction,
because it may remove safepoint insns. We really want to insert PPs as
late as possible since once they're in nothing removes them.

Doing it in a pass may require dominance info to get right. Consider
yarv insns expanding to a diamond and loops.

commit_message:
gh-150505: fix data race in Unpickler_set_memo under free-threading

Unpickler_set_memo modified self->memo and self->memo_size without any
critical section, allowing concurrent threads to race on the same
Unpickler instance. Wrap the memo population loop and the pointer swap
in Py_BEGIN_CRITICAL_SECTION/Py_END_CRITICAL_SECTION to serialize
access.

As previously discussed with @ncoghlan and approved for 3.15b2 by @hugovk,

gh-150228: Improve the PEP 829 batch processing APIs

As previously discussed with @ncoghlan and approved for 3.15b2 by @hugovk,
this exposes the batch processing APIs for addsitedir() and friends.  We
remove the `defer_processing_start_files` flag which required some implicit
module global state, and promote StartupState to the public documented API.
This removes the need for module global implicit state and allows callers to
control when accumulated .start and .pth file state is processed if they want.

This also fixes the interleaving regression identified by @ncoghlan in the
same issue.  Now, .pth file sys.path extensions are added to sys.path after
the sitedir that the .pth file is found in, restoring the legacy behavior.

  Use *args to accept any number of arguments.

  Fixes #150484
